classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate a reciprocal function, compare tangent gradients, find two tangent equations and their intersection, and sketch the configuration.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the tangents to $f(x)=\dfrac{12}{x}$ at $M(2,6)$ and $T(-2,-6)$ are parallel.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=-\frac{12}{x^2}\\f'(2)&=-\frac{12}{2^2}=-3\\f'(-2)&=-\frac{12}{(-2)^2}=-3\end{align*}$$
Both tangents have gradient $-3$, so they are parallel.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the tangents at $M(2,6)$ and $N(6,2)$ and their point of intersection.

answer.worked:
At $M$, the gradient is $-3$:
$$\begin{align*}y-6&=-3(x-2)\\y&=-3x+12\end{align*}$$
At $N$:
$$\begin{align*}f'(6)&=-\frac{12}{6^2}=-\frac13\\y-2&=-\frac13(x-6)\\y&=-\frac13x+4\end{align*}$$
At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}-3x+12&=-\frac13x+4\\-9x+36&=-x+12\\8x&=24\\x&=3\\y&=-3(3)+12=3\end{align*}$$
The tangents intersect at $(3,3)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch the situation in part b.

answer.short: The sketch shows $y=\frac{12}{x}$ and its tangents at $M$ and $N$.
answer.worked: Sketch the reciprocal curve in quadrants I and III. Mark $M(2,6)$ and $N(6,2)$ on the positive branch. Draw $y=-3x+12$ through $M$ and $y=-\tfrac13x+4$ through $N$; the tangents intersect at $(3,3)$.

spec.description: Editable equation-driven reciprocal graph with two tangent lines, labelled M and N, double-ended axes and continuation arrows; no numerical ticks. Source series colours distinguish the curve and the two tangents.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=12/x; M=(2,6), N=(6,2); tangents y=-3x+12 and y=-x/3+4 intersect at (3,3).
